title: Kimi K3 vs Claude Fable 5 on DeepSWE: Cost and Coding
gist: Together AI benchmarked open-weight Kimi K3 against Claude Fable 5 at its xhigh setting on DeepSWE across 452 graded rollouts: Fable leads pass@1 69.9% to 68.5%, but Kimi wins pass@2 (82.0 vs 80.2) and pass@4 (89.4% vs 88.5%) while costing $4.65 per rollout versus $13.41 - 2.8x more solved tasks per dollar. The two models are unusually correlated (0.72 per task, the highest cross-vendor similarity in the benchmark), so pairing them buys almost no coverage diversity.

insights.claim: On DeepSWE official scoring Claude Fable 5 at xhigh solves 69.9 percent of tasks on the first try versus 68.5 percent for Kimi K3 at max effort - a 1.4 point gap between an open-weight model and Anthropic's flagship.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: A 1.4-point quality gap is inside the noise band for most production coding use, which removes quality as the reason to pay closed-model prices.
insights.quote: Fable xhigh solves 69.9% of tasks on the first try under DeepSWE’s official scoring. Kimi K3 max solves 68.5%.
insights.locator: The DeepSWE scoreboard: pass@1 and pass@k

insights.claim: The ranking flips at higher k: Kimi K3 leads pass@2 82.0 versus 80.2 and pass@4 89.4 percent versus Fable's 88.5, with only two cheap GPT configs (Luna max and GPT-5.5 high at 90.3) ever reaching higher across the 44-config export.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: For retry-tolerant agent workflows the open model is already the best-in-class choice, not merely the cheap choice.
insights.locator: Also when you allow for larger pass@k's the ranking flips

insights.claim: Kimi K3's arrival represents a +38 point leap over the prior release, the largest between-model-release jump in the entire DeepSWE dataset.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: The size of the generational jump is the strongest evidence that open-weight capability is compounding faster than closed-model capability.
insights.quote: the K3 +38 point leap is the largest between model releases in this entire dataset.
insights.locator: One point four between an open-weight model

insights.claim: The comparison rests on 452 graded rollouts landed July 16, 2026 - 113 long-horizon feature requests from live open-source repos, four trials each, graded pass/fail by a hidden test suite - and the authors note the figures can differ from other public scorecards.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Methodology disclosure matters: these are vendor-run numbers on one specific configuration, not a neutral consensus leaderboard.
insights.locator: Kimi K3 landed in DeepSWE on July 16, 2026

insights.claim: Kimi K3 costs $4.65 per DeepSWE rollout against $13.41 for Claude Fable 5 at xhigh, making the full 452-rollout sweep $2,103 versus $6,010.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: A roughly 3x unit-cost gap at near-parity quality is the concrete number that drives enterprise migration off closed models.
insights.quote: Kimi K3: $4.65 per rollout. Fable xhigh: $13.41. The full 452-rollout sweep: $2,103 vs $6,010.
insights.locator: Cost comparison: Kimi K3 vs Claude Fable 5 pricing

insights.claim: Measured per solved task, Kimi K3 delivers 14.7 solves per $100 versus Claude Fable 5's 5.3, about 2.8x the work per dollar.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Solves-per-dollar is the right unit for budgeting agentic coding workloads and shows the cost gap survives adjusting for quality.
insights.quote: Per solved task, Kimi delivers 14.7 solves per $100 versus Fable’s 5.3 - 2.8x the work per dollar.
insights.locator: Per solved task, Kimi delivers 14.7 solves per $100

insights.claim: The authors conclude Kimi K3 is now the rational default, offering near-flagship reach and the best pass@4 of any flagship-tier config at 35 cents on Claude Fable 5's dollar.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: An explicit vendor recommendation to switch defaults - note the publisher is an inference provider that monetizes open-model serving.
insights.quote: Kimi K3 is now the rational default: near-flagship reach, the best pass@4 of any flagship-tier config, at 35 cents on Fable’s dollar.

insights.claim: Kimi K3 takes much longer wall-clock time than Claude Fable 5, which the authors expect to improve once the model is open sourced and inference is optimized.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Latency, not cost or quality, is the remaining gap - and it is precisely the gap an inference provider like Together AI is positioned to close.
insights.quote: Kimi takes a much longer time but this will no doubt improve when the model is open sourced and inference is optimized!
insights.locator: Kimi takes a much longer time

insights.claim: Decomposing pass@1 shows Kimi K3 reaches 89.4 percent of the DeepSWE benchmark with only 12 tasks it never cracks against Fable's 13, the highest coverage peak in the dataset, but is less reliable at 76.6 percent versus Fable's 79.0 percent.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Coverage-versus-reliability is the right lens for model selection: wide-net models suit retry loops, deterministic models suit single-shot production paths.

insights.claim: Claude Fable 5 solves 58 tasks four-for-four against Kimi K3's 45, making Fable the steadier and more deterministic model while Kimi casts the wider net.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Determinism has real operational value in unattended agent pipelines where a retry is expensive or impossible - a reason to keep paying for the closed model on some paths.
insights.quote: Fable is steadier and more deterministic; Kimi is the wider net, which accounts for its gains at pass@2 and @4.

insights.claim: Per-task correlation between Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5 is 0.72, the highest cross-vendor similarity in the entire benchmark, and the top four cross-vendor similarities in the export are all Kimi-K3-versus-Anthropic pairs.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: High cross-vendor correlation suggests convergent training approaches and undermines the diversification rationale for multi-vendor model stacks.
insights.quote: Per-task correlation between Kimi K3 and Fable is 0.72 - the highest cross-vendor similarity in the entire benchmark.
insights.locator: How similar are Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5?

insights.claim: There is not a single task where one of Kimi K3 or Claude Fable 5 goes four-for-four while the other goes zero-for-four in either direction, a first across every pairing the authors have analyzed.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: The absence of complementary blind spots is unusually strong evidence the two models have effectively the same capability surface.
insights.locator: There is not a single task where one goes four-for-four

insights.claim: Pairing Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5 buys almost no diversity: their union covers 105 of 113 tasks, barely above Kimi alone at 101, with both solving 96 tasks, Kimi adding 5 alone, Fable adding 4 alone, and the same 8 resisting both.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Kills the router or ensemble arbitrage between these two specific models - pay for one, not both.
insights.quote: their union covers 105 of 113 tasks, barely above Kimi alone at 101.
insights.locator: In practice, Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5 succeed and fail

insights.claim: The two models share failure anatomies as well: 65 percent of failures are near misses for both, and both protect the repository's existing test suite with 11 percent versus 10 percent baseline regressions.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Similar regression discipline means the open model carries no extra code-safety risk, removing a common objection to switching.

insights.claim: By programming language Kimi K3 takes Go decisively 79 to 71 while Claude Fable 5 holds Python 74-68, JavaScript 70-65, TypeScript 64-60, and Rust 75-65.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Language-level splits let teams route by stack rather than adopting one model wholesale - the practical way to capture most of the cost saving.
insights.quote: Kimi takes Go decisively (79 vs 71). Fable holds the other four: Python 74-68, JavaScript 70-65, TypeScript 64-60, and Rust 75-65.
insights.locator: Kimi K3 vs Fable 5 by programming language

insights.claim: The authors highlight how far Kimi K3 has closed the Rust gap with Claude Fable 5, noting no other model including GPT 5.6 Sol is as good at Rust.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Rust competence has been a durable closed-model advantage; its erosion signals the remaining moats are narrow and shrinking.
insights.locator: The really interesting detail here is how much K3 catches up

insights.claim: Kimi K3 is an open-weight model from Moonshot AI that can be self-hosted or served through inference providers once weights are released, while Claude Fable 5 is closed and available only through Anthropic and its partners.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Deployment control, not just price, is the structural argument for open weights - and it is the business Together AI is selling into.
